# Job Chapter 32 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 428r–428v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JOB_032_page_001.jpg, JOB_032_page_002.jpg

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** So these three men ceased to answer Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.

**2** Then the anger of Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram, was kindled. His anger burned against Job because he justified himself rather than God.

**3** His anger also burned against his three friends because they had found no answer, although they had declared Job to be in the wrong.

**4** Now Elihu had waited to speak to Job because they were older than he.

**5** And when Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of these three men, his anger was kindled.

**6** And Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said: "I am young in years, and you are aged; therefore I held back and was afraid to share my knowledge with you.

**7** I thought, 'Let days speak, and many years make wisdom known.'

**8** But truly it is the spirit in a person, the breath of the Almighty, that gives understanding.

**9** It is not only the great who are wise, nor only the aged who understand what is right.

**10** Therefore I say, 'Listen to me; let me also declare my opinion.'

**11** Behold, I waited for your words; I listened for your wise arguments while you searched for what to say.

**12** I paid close attention, and behold, there was none among you who refuted Job or who answered his words.

**13** Beware of saying, 'We have found wisdom; God may refute him, not a man.'

**14** He has not directed his words against me, and I will not answer him with your arguments.

**15** They are dismayed; they answer no more; they have not a word to say.

**16** And shall I wait because they do not speak, because they stand there and answer no more?

**17** I also will give my answer; I also will declare what I know.

**18** For I am full of words; the spirit within me compels me.

**19** Behold, my belly is like wine that has no vent; like new wineskins it is ready to burst.

**20** I must speak so that I may find relief; I must open my lips and answer.

**21** I will not show partiality to any person, nor will I flatter anyone,

**22** for I do not know how to flatter; if I did, my Maker would soon take me away."

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

Job 32 marks a major structural turning point. The three-friend dialogue cycle has collapsed — Bildad's speech shrank to six verses, Zophar never appeared for his third round, and now all three fall silent. Into this vacuum steps Elihu, an entirely new character with no prior introduction. The prose frame (vv.1-5) is the first narrator speech since chapter 2, and it emphasizes Elihu's anger with remarkable intensity — the word *charah* ("burned") appears four times. Elihu is angry at Job for self-justification and at the friends for their failure to answer. His speech in vv.6-22 is largely preamble — he talks about talking, explains why he will speak, and compares himself to a wineskin about to burst. The actual substance of his argument will come in chapters 33-37. Whether Elihu is the author's final wisdom voice or a later addition, his structural function is clear: he delays the divine theophany, building anticipation for God's own answer in chapter 38.

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.3 — "they had condemned Job" — Tiqqun Sopherim
- **EMET:** notes the scribal tradition that the original read "they had condemned God"
- **LOGOS:** "they had declared Job to be in the wrong" (follows MT)
- **PNEUMA:** "they had condemned him" (follows MT)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** Follow the MT text ("they had declared Job to be in the wrong"). The tiqqun sopherim tradition is noted in EMET's apparatus as an important textual variant but should not alter the consensus translation.

### V.8 — "the spirit in a man" vs. "the spirit God puts in a person"
- **EMET:** "the-spirit [ruach] in-man [enosh]"
- **LOGOS:** "the spirit in a man"
- **PNEUMA:** "the spirit God puts in a person"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "the spirit in a person" — the Hebrew says simply "spirit in man." PNEUMA's "God puts" is interpretive (though contextually implied by the parallel "breath of the Almighty").

### V.19 — "my belly" vs. "my stomach" vs. "my insides"
- **EMET:** "my-belly [vitni]"
- **LOGOS:** "my stomach"
- **PNEUMA:** "my insides"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "my belly" — *beten* is a concrete bodily term. "Stomach" is too clinical; "insides" is too vague. "Belly" preserves the visceral quality of Elihu's image.

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
